On The Local Well-Posedness for Some Systems of Coupled KdV EquationsThanks: 1Initially supported by FAPESP/Brazil grant No. 2002/02522-0, and later by CNRS/France.Thanks: 2Supported by FAPESP under grant No. 2002/08920-7.Thanks: Date: October 2005.

Abstract.

Using the theory developed by Kenig, Ponce, and Vega, we prove that the Hirota-Satsuma system is locally well-posed in Sobolev spaces Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for 3/4<s≤13/4<s\leq 1. We introduce some Bourgain-type spaces Xs,baX_{s,b}^{a} for a≠0a\not=0, s,b∈ℝs,b\in\mathbb{R} to obtain local well-posedness for the Gear-Grimshaw system in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for s>−3/4s>-3/4, by establishing new mixed-bilinear estimates involving the two Bourgain-type spaces Xs,b−α−X_{s,b}^{-\alpha_{-}} and Xs,b−α+X_{s,b}^{-\alpha_{+}} adapted to ∂t+α−∂x3\partial_{t}+\alpha_{-}\partial_{x}^{3} and ∂t+α+∂x3\partial_{t}+\alpha_{+}\partial_{x}^{3} respectively, where |α+|=|α−|≠0|\alpha_{+}|=|\alpha_{-}|\not=0.

MSC: 35A07; 35Q53

Keywords: Hirota-Satsuma system; Gear-Grimshaw system; KdV equation

1. Introduction

In this paper we are concerned with two systems of coupled KdV equations, namely the Hirota-Satsuma system and the Gear-Grimshaw system.

First we consider local well-posedness (LWP) and ill-posedness of the initial value problem (IVP) for the following system:

{ut−a⁡(ux​x​x+6​u​ux)=2​b​v​vx,vt+vx​x​x+3​u​vx=0,u(0)=u0,v(0)=v0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}-a(u_{xxx}+6uu_{x})=2bvv_{x},\\ v_{t}+v_{xxx}+3uv_{x}=0,\\ u(0)=u_{0},\;\;v(0)=v_{0},\end{array}\right. (1.1)

known as the Hirota-Satsuma system which was introduced in [10] to describe the interaction of two long waves with different dispersion relations. Here a,ba,b are real constants, and u,vu,v are real-valued functions of the two real variables xx and tt. System (1.1) is a set of coupled Korteweg-de Vries (abbreviated KdV henceforth) equations, and it is a generalization of the KdV equation (which is obtained when v=0v=0). The Cauchy problem associated to (1.1), for the real and periodic case, was previously studied by P. F. He [9], for b>0b>0, −1<a<0-1<a<0, and considering Sobolev indices s≥3s\geq 3. It deserves remark that system (1.1) has the following conserved quantities:

V⁡(u,v)\displaystyle V(u,v) =\displaystyle= ∫−∞+∞(1+a2​ux2+b​vx2−(1+a)​u3−b​u​v2)​𝑑x,\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\Big(\frac{1+a}{2}u_{x}^{2}+bv_{x}^{2}-(1+a)u^{3}-buv^{2}\Big)dx, (1.2)
F⁡(u,v)\displaystyle F(u,v) =\displaystyle= ∫−∞+∞(u2+23​b​v2)​𝑑x.\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\big(u^{2}+\frac{2}{3}bv^{2}\big)dx. (1.3)

Later, Feng [6] considered the initial value problem for the following system:

{ut−a⁡(ux​x​x+6​u​ux)=2​b​v​vx,vt+vx​x​x+c​u​vx+d​v​vx=0,u(0)=u0,v(0)=v0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}-a(u_{xxx}+6uu_{x})=2bvv_{x},\\ v_{t}+v_{xxx}+cuv_{x}+dvv_{x}=0,\\ u(0)=u_{0},\;\;v(0)=v_{0},\end{array}\right. (1.4)

which reduces to the Hirota-Satsuma system when c=3c=3 and d=0d=0, always assuming that a≠0a\not=0. LWP of the IVP associated to system (1.4) was obtained, for initial data (u0,v0)∈Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)(u_{0},v_{0})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for s≥1s\geq 1, with a+1≠0a+1\not=0 and b​c>0bc>0. Moreover, global well-posedness (GWP) for system (1.4) was also proved (see [6]) in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for s≥1s\geq 1, if −1<a<0-1<a<0 and b​c>0bc>0.

The second problem we will consider here is related to the local well-posedness of the IVP for the Gear-Grimshaw system given by

{ut+ux​x​x+a3​vx​x​x+u​ux+a1​v​vx+a2​(u​v)x=0,b1​vt+vx​x​x+b2​a3​ux​x​x+v​vx+b2​a2​u​ux+b2​a1​(u​v)x+r​vx=0,u(0)=u0,v(0)=v0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}+u_{xxx}+a_{3}v_{xxx}+uu_{x}+a_{1}vv_{x}+a_{2}(uv)_{x}=0,\\ b_{1}v_{t}+v_{xxx}+b_{2}a_{3}u_{xxx}+vv_{x}+b_{2}a_{2}uu_{x}+b_{2}a_{1}(uv)_{x}+rv_{x}=0,\\ u(0)=u_{0},\;\;v(0)=v_{0},\end{array}\right. (1.5)

where a1,a2,a3∈ℝa_{1},a_{2},a_{3}\in\mathbb{R}, r∈ℝr\in\mathbb{R}, and b1,b2>0b_{1},b_{2}>0; u=u⁡(x,t)u=u(x,t), v=v⁡(x,t)v=v(x,t) are real-valued functions of the two real variables xx and tt. System (1.5) was derived in [7] (see also [3] for a very good explanation about the physical context in which this system arises) as a model to describe the strong interaction of two-dimensional, weakly nonlinear, long, internal gravity waves propagating on neighboring pycnoclines in a stratified fluid, where the two waves correspond to different modes. Bona et al. [3] proved GWP of the IVP associated to (1.5) with initial data belonging to Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for s≥1s\geq 1, assuming r=0r=0 and |a3|<1/b2|a_{3}|<1/\sqrt{b_{2}}. Later, Ash et al. [1] considered GWP of (1.5) in L2​(ℝ)×L2​(ℝ)L^{2}(\mathbb{R})\times L^{2}(\mathbb{R}) supposing r=0r=0 and |a3|≠1/b2|a_{3}|\not=1/\sqrt{b_{2}} (see Section 3.1-(2)). Further, Saut and Tzvetkov [17] considered GWP of system (3.1) for initial data (u0,v0)∈L2​(ℝ)×L2​(ℝ)(u_{0},v_{0})\in L^{2}(\mathbb{R})\times L^{2}(\mathbb{R}), assuming that r≠0r\not=0 and that the matrix (ai​j)i,j∈{1,2}(a_{ij})_{i,j\in\{1,2\}} has real distinct eigenvalues (see Section 3.1-(1)). Recently, Linares and Panthee [15], by using the bilinear estimate of Kenig, Ponce, and Vega [13], showed LWP for system (3.5) with initial data (u0,v0)∈Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)(u_{0},v_{0})\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for s>−3/4s>-3/4 (see Section 3.1-(2), and Remark 3.1-ii.)). Solutions of (1.5) satisfy the following conservation laws:

Φ1​(u)=∫−∞+∞u​𝑑x,Φ2​(v)=∫−∞+∞v​𝑑x,Φ3​(u,v)=∫−∞+∞(b2​u2+b1​v2)​𝑑x,\Phi_{1}(u)=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}udx,\,\,\,\Phi_{2}(v)=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}vdx,\,\,\,\Phi_{3}(u,v)=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}(b_{2}u^{2}+b_{1}v^{2})dx,
Φ4​(u,v)=∫−∞+∞(b2​ux2+vx2+2​b2​a3​ux​vx−b2​u33−b2​a2​u2​v−b2​a1​u​v2−v33−r​v2)​𝑑x.\Phi_{4}(u,v)=\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty}\Big(b_{2}u_{x}^{2}+v_{x}^{2}+2b_{2}a_{3}u_{x}v_{x}-b_{2}\frac{u^{3}}{3}-b_{2}a_{2}u^{2}v-b_{2}a_{1}uv^{2}-\frac{v^{3}}{3}-rv^{2}\Big)dx.

We say that the IVP

{∂tu→​(t)=F⁡(t,u→​(t)),u→​(0)=u→0\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}\partial_{t}\vec{u}(t)=F(t,\vec{u}(t)),\\ \vec{u}(0)=\vec{u}_{0}\end{array}\right.

is locally well-posed in XX (Banach space) if there exist T=T⁡(‖u→0‖X)>0T=T(\|\vec{u}_{0}\|_{X})>0 and a unique solution u→​(t)\vec{u}(t) of the corresponding IVP such that
i.) u→∈C⁡([−T,T],X)∩YT=XT\vec{u}\in C([-T,T];X)\cap Y_{T}=X_{T};
ii.) the mapping data-solution u→0↦u→​(t)\vec{u}_{0}\mapsto\vec{u}(t), from {v→0∈X;‖v→0‖X≤M}\{\vec{v}_{0}\in X;\|\vec{v}_{0}\|_{X}\leq M\} into XTX_{T} is uniformly continuous for all M>0M>0; i.e.

∀M>0,∀ϵ>0,∃δ=δ⁡(ϵ,M)>0,‖u→0−v→0‖X<δ​then​‖u→−v→‖XT<ϵ,\displaystyle\forall M>0,\forall\epsilon>0,\exists\delta=\delta(\epsilon,M)>0,\|\vec{u}_{0}-\vec{v}_{0}\|_{X}<\delta\;\;\text{then}\;\;\|\vec{u}-\vec{v}\|_{X_{T}}<\epsilon,
where​‖u→0‖X≤M​and​‖v→0‖X≤M.\displaystyle\text{where}\;\;\|\vec{u}_{0}\|_{X}\leq M\;\;\text{and}\;\;\|\vec{v}_{0}\|_{X}\leq M.

We say that the IVP is globally well-posed in XX if the same properties hold for all time T>0T>0. If some hypothesis in the definition of local well-posedness fails, we say that the IVP is ill-posed.

This paper is organized as follows. In Section 2 we use Banach’s fixed-point theorem in a suitable function space and the theory obtained by Kenig, Ponce, and Vega, to prove LWP to system (1.1), for any a,b∈ℝa,b\in\mathbb{R}, with initial data in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for 3/4<s≤13/4<s\leq 1. We also show that system (1.1) with a≠0a\not=0 is ill-posed in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs′​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s^{\prime}}(\mathbb{R}) for s∈[−1,−34)s\in[-1,-\frac{3}{4}), and s′∈ℝs^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}. We begin Section 3 with a few comments to scale changes carried out previously concerning the Gear-Grimshaw system. Thus, we introduce some Bourgain-type spaces Xs,baX_{s,b}^{a} for a≠0a\not=0, and s,b∈ℝs,b\in\mathbb{R}. Moreover, we prove some new mixed-bilinear estimates involving the two Bourgain-type spaces Xs,b1X_{s,b}^{1} and Xs,b−1X_{s,b}^{-1} corresponding to ∂t−∂x3\partial_{t}-\partial_{x}^{3} and ∂t+∂x3\partial_{t}+\partial_{x}^{3} respectively, to obtain LWP for the Gear-Grimshaw system (3.1) with r=0r=0, a12=a21=0a_{12}=a_{21}=0, a11=−a22≠0a_{11}=-a_{22}\not=0, and initial data in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s}(\mathbb{R}) for s>−3/4s>-3/4 (see Theorem 3.2 below). We remark that these mixed-bilinear estimates (see Proposition 3.2) presented here are not an immediate consequence of the estimates proved by Kenig, Ponce, and Vega in [13] (see Remark 3.2 and Remark 3.4-ii.)). Finally, we notice that system (1.1) is treated separately from system (1.5) because the nonlinearity in (1.1) has the non-divergence form, while the one in (1.5) has the divergence form; a possible difficulty with regard to the LWP of (1.1) in lower Sobolev indices could be related to the obtention of a suitable bilinear estimate for the nonlinear term in the second equation of (1.1).

2. On the Hirota-Satsuma System

2.1. Local Well-Posedness

Let us denote by

Ua(t)=eat∂x3,Ua​(t)​ϕ^(ξ)=e−i​a​t​ξ3ϕ^(ξ)forϕ∈Hs(ℝ),U_{a}(t)=e^{at\partial_{x}^{3}},\;\;\;\widehat{U_{a}(t)\phi}(\xi)=e^{-iat\xi^{3}}\hat{\phi}(\xi)\;\;\text{for}\;\;\phi\in H^{s}(\mathbb{R}), (2.1)

the group associated with the linear part of the first equation of system (1.1). We note that U​(t)≡U−1​(t)U(t)\equiv U_{-1}(t) is the group associated with the linear part of the KdV equation. Next theorem proves LWP to system (1.1) in suitable Sobolev spaces.

Remark 2.1.

In [16], Sakovich considered the following system:

{ux​x​x+a​u​ux+b​v​ux+c​u​vx+d​v​vx+m​ut+n​vt=0,vx​x​x+e​u​ux+f​v​ux+g​u​vx+h​v​vx+p​ut+q​vt=0,u(0)=u0,v(0)=v0,\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{xxx}+auu_{x}+bvu_{x}+cuv_{x}+dvv_{x}+mu_{t}+nv_{t}=0,\\ v_{xxx}+euu_{x}+fvu_{x}+guv_{x}+hvv_{x}+pu_{t}+qv_{t}=0,\\ u(0)=u_{0},\;\;v(0)=v_{0},\end{array}\right. (2.21)

where m​q≠n​pmq\neq np. This system can be written as

(ux​x​xvx​x​x)+A0​(u​uxv​ux)+A1​(u​vxv​vx)+A2​(utvt)=0,\displaystyle\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{c}u_{xxx}\\ v_{xxx}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)+A_{0}\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{c}uu_{x}\\ vu_{x}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)+A_{1}\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{c}uv_{x}\\ vv_{x}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)+A_{2}\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{c}u_{t}\\ v_{t}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)=0,

where

A0=(abef),A1=(cdgh),A2=(mnpq).\displaystyle A_{0}=\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}a&b\\ e&f\end{array}\right),\;A_{1}=\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}c&d\\ g&h\end{array}\right),\;A_{2}=\left(\begin{array}[]{cc}m&n\\ p&q\end{array}\right).

Since A2A_{2} is nonsingular, multiplying (2.1) by A2−1A_{2}^{-1}, we get

(utvt)+A2−1​(ux​x​xvx​x​x)+A2−1​A0​(u​uxv​ux)+A2−1​A1​(u​vxv​vx)=0.\displaystyle\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{cc}u_{t}\\ v_{t}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)+A_{2}^{-1}\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{cc}u_{xxx}\\ v_{xxx}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)+A_{2}^{-1}A_{0}\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{cc}uu_{x}\\ vu_{x}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)+A_{2}^{-1}A_{1}\left(\!\!\begin{array}[]{cc}uv_{x}\\ vv_{x}\end{array}\!\!\!\right)=0.

If P∈G​L​(2)P\in GL(2) is such that P−1​A2−1​P=diag​(a0,a1)P^{-1}A_{2}^{-1}P=\text{diag}(a_{0},a_{1}), where a0a_{0} and a1a_{1} are the eigenvalues of A2−1A_{2}^{-1}, by making U=(u,v)t=P​VU=(u,v)^{t}=PV, we obtain a new system of Hirota-Satsuma type. Therefore, similar results to Theorems 2.1 and 2.2 are also valid for this new system.

2.2. Ill-Posedness to the Hirota-Satsuma System

Let us remark that if u⁡(x,t)u(x,t) and v⁡(x,t)v(x,t) are solutions of (1.1), then u~​(x,t)=λ2​u​(λ​x,λ3​t)\tilde{u}(x,t)=\lambda^{2}u(\lambda x,\lambda^{3}t) and v~​(x,t)=λ2​v​(λ​x,λ3​t)\tilde{v}(x,t)=\lambda^{2}v(\lambda x,\lambda^{3}t) are also solutions of (1.1). This scaling argument suggests that the Cauchy problem for the Hirota-Satsuma system is locally well-posed in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs′​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s^{\prime}}(\mathbb{R}) for s,s′>−32s,s^{\prime}>-\frac{3}{2}. It is not difficult to see that the IVP associated to the KdV equation

{wt+wx​x​x+6​w​wx=0,w​(x,0)=w0​(x)\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}w_{t}+w_{xxx}+6ww_{x}=0,\\ w(x,0)=w_{0}(x)\end{array}\right.

is equivalent to the IVP

{ut−a⁡(ux​x​x+6​u​ux)=0,u⁡(x,0)=u0​(x)=w0​(−x),\left\{\begin{array}[]{l}u_{t}-a(u_{xxx}+6uu_{x})=0,\\ u(x,0)=u_{0}(x)=w_{0}(-x),\end{array}\right. (2.30)

through the transformation u⁡(x,t)=w⁡(−x,a​t)u(x,t)=w(-x,at), for a≠0a\not=0. Note that if uu is a solution of (2.30), then (u,0)(u,0) is a solution of problem (1.1) with initial data (u0,0)(u_{0},0). Then, it follows from the ill-posedness result for the KdV equation (see [5]) that the mapping data-solution associated to the IVP (1.1) with a≠0a\not=0 is not uniformly continuous in Hs​(ℝ)×Hs′​(ℝ)H^{s}(\mathbb{R})\times H^{s^{\prime}}(\mathbb{R}), for s∈[−1,−34)s\in[-1,-\frac{3}{4}), and s′∈ℝs^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}.

3.5. Future Work

Suppose a,a′∈ℝ∖{0}a,a^{\prime}\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\} and |a|≠|a′||a|\not=|a^{\prime}|. We remark that an interesting problem for a future research is to determine whether or not Proposition 3.2 is still true when we replace the super-indices 11 by aa and −1-1 by a′a^{\prime}. We point out that this result (in general) is not an immediate consequence of the calculations we did here for proving Propositions 3.1 or 3.2 or from the calculations done in [13] to prove Corollary 2.7-[13]. This result would let us to prove LWP for the Gear-Grimshaw system (3.1) with r=0r=0, when a12=a21=0a_{12}=a_{21}=0, |a11|≠|a22||a_{11}|\not=|a_{22}|, and a11,a22∈ℝ∖{0}a_{11},a_{22}\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}. Moreover, if this result is true, we also could obtain LWP for system (3.1) with r=0r=0, when A=(ai​j)∼diag​(α+,α−)A=(a_{ij})\sim\text{diag}(\alpha_{+},\alpha_{-}), where α+\alpha_{+} and α−\alpha_{-} are the eigenvalues of AA with α+,α−∈ℝ∖{0}\alpha_{+},\alpha_{-}\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}, |α+|≠|α−||\alpha_{+}|\not=|\alpha_{-}|.
